paragraphs: Friend, here's what sticks with me. Ahab had a palace, a crown and a whole kingdom, and he lay on his bed with his face turned away over one vegetable garden (1 Kings 21:2, 4). Naboth said no because it was the inheritance of his fathers (1 Kings 21:3). Wanting what isn't yours is a small seed, and this passage shows how big that seed can grow when nobody pulls it up.

Now look at who saw it all. Naboth's death came with letters, a fast, a seat of honor and the people watching, so it was made to look proper (1 Kings 21:8-13). But the word of the LORD came to Elijah, and God asked, "Have you not murdered a man and seized his land?" (1 Kings 21:19). Nothing done in secret is secret to Him, and the LORD cared about Naboth when it looked like nobody else did.

And then comes the part I can't get over. Ahab tore his clothes, put on sackcloth and walked around meekly (1 Kings 21:27), and the LORD said, "Have you seen how Ahab has humbled himself before Me?" (1 Kings 21:29). Humbling yourself before God matters to Him, and I know a little about being low and needing Him to reach down. The story isn't over for Ahab, though, so keep your oven warm, friend.
